solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Energetically jovial team members having a drink

parts.note: backs are players in the defensive positions of a rugby or football team
lapping is drinking with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Some sportspeople are cheerfully sharing a drink together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty back-slapping is the over-enthusiastic chumminess of someone being boisterously friendly.

clue.text: She sponsors France's best exhibitions at first, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says these letters end up arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word exhibitions

explanation.surface: A woman backs the finest French art shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal at the end rearranges FRANCES, BEST and E, the first letter of exhibitions picked by 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female patron who gives money to support a cause is a sponsoring woman, so the definition describes her role.

clue.text: Tory ultimately organising a dance

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word organising

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician ends up arranging a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin American party dance is performed in a long snaking line of people.

clue.text: Bag carried by friends at Chelsea

indicators.note: carried by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone's bag is being looked after by pals at a London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London district and football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolchild's shoulder bag with a flap is the classic example of this kind of carrier.

clue.text: Birds' enclosure originally accessed by means of railway

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word accessed

parts.note: via means by way of or through

explanation.surface: A zoo's bird house was first reached by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cage or building where birds are kept is exactly what the definition describes.

clue.text: Songbird Greek character buried in mine

indicators.note: buried in says one piece sits inside the other, as if underground

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A singing bird and a Greek person are trapped underground in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown bird of fields and moorland is a member of the singing bird family.

clue.text: Lacking capacity to be distinguished

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the answer says incapable or unfit

explanation.surface: Being unable to do something can make you stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the letters say incapable; whole, they mean eminent or remarkable.

clue.text: Disunity of odd blokes in sci-fi film

indicators.note: in says the words before sit inside the film's title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's science-fiction film about an alien
odd means strange
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Weird men in a science-fiction movie fall out with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out that leaves people apart and unfriendly is a breakdown of unity.

clue.text: Northern town initially housing a single music group

indicators.note: housing says the next piece is held inside the letters before it
initially points to the opening letter of the word town

parts.note: a single means one

explanation.surface: A town in the north first hosts one band.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians is a specific size of ensemble, like a trio or quartet.

clue.text: Momentum of this writer's dog, perhaps (American)

parts.note: the writer refers to themself as I, and this writer's (I am) contracts to I'm
a dog is an example of a pet
US means American

explanation.surface: The setter's American dog has plenty of drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving force or forward thrust is what both words describe.

clue.text: Old man grabbing eastern bird's plume

indicators.note: grabbing says the first piece seizes and holds the next one inside

parts.note: old man is slang for father

explanation.surface: An elderly man snatches a plume from an eastern bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are covered in plumes, the single quill-and-vane structures of their plumage.

clue.text: Drum mostly banned by Rossini at first

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taboo means forbidden or banned

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word Rossini

explanation.surface: A drum was largely forbidden by the Italian opera composer Rossini.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drum played with one hand, often alongside a pipe, in early music.

clue.text: Attractive liberal replacing daughter in light entertainment

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: comedy is light entertainment

explanation.surface: A good-looking Liberal politician steps in for a daughter in a comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant to look at is an old-fashioned synonym for good-looking or pretty.

clue.text: Move abroad, developing ragtime

indicators.note: developing says the letters of ragtime grow into something new

explanation.surface: Ragtime music spreads overseas as it develops.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate to another country, as people or birds do, is to move abroad.

clue.text: Beware of sailors in underground chamber

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, used as a warning in old school slang
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A warning about sailors lurking in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' (pronounced KAY-vee) was British schoolboy slang for 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cave or hollow below ground is a subterranean room.

clue.text: Attack an old sailor picked up by the ears?

indicators.note: picked up by the ears means heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor is assaulted by being grabbed by the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent strike or onslaught on someone is an attack.

clue.text: Tiresome type carrying note round Pacific island

indicators.note: carrying says the first piece holds the next one within it

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tedious person takes a message to a South Seas island.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island in the Malay Archipelago lies in the western Pacific region.

clue.text: Correct liturgy for listeners?

indicators.note: for listeners says the word counts as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a rite is a liturgical ceremony

explanation.surface: A proper church service is being performed to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate or true, as in giving an answer that is not wrong.

clue.text: Article I digested on female — one with taking ways?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows
digested says the piece is swallowed inside the word before it

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A news piece on a woman digests a story about someone charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ways' usually means charm, but here it means taking things that are not yours.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals has a habit of taking things, a joking twist on charming manners.

clue.text: Old part of play bishop held to be indecent

indicators.note: held says the bishop is kept inside the letters around it

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An old scene with a bishop is judged improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive to accepted standards of decency, especially sexually explicit.

clue.text: Exceptionally wide, for example

definitions.meaning: very or unusually, as in especially large
in cricket a wide is a run scored for a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, counted apart from the batters' own runs

explanation.surface: Something is unusually broad, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a bonus run awarded for a ball bowled out of reach.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means especially; in cricket it names any run not scored off the bat, such as a wide.

clue.text: Eg Victoria's position in life?

definitions.meaning: Victoria is a major London railway terminus
one's rank or standing in society

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's standing in society.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria suggests the queen, but it is the London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway terminus is a stop; social rank is one's standing.

clue.text: Release United fan finally before match

indicators.note: before says these letters come ahead of the next piece

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word fan

parts.note: a tie is a cup match in football

explanation.surface: A United supporter is let go just before the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or undo a knot is to set something free.

clue.text: Number one painting?

parts.note: number one is slang for oneself, so this is a picture an artist paints of their own person, not a top-ranked canvas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' suggests a best work, but means oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's portrait of themselves depicts the painter as subject.
